The bars are specific fertility rates (per 1000 women). Move the two peak groups and watch the total fertility rate.

title: Generations of mothers: GRR and NRR

sliders.name: sv
sliders.label: Survival ratio of girls to motherhood

preset.caption: Start with 1000 women. GRR counts the daughters they would bear (TFR × share of girls). NRR also allows for daughters who die before they reach the child-bearing ages (× survival ratio). Press Next generation: each generation of mothers is NRR times the last.
preset.title: Generations of mothers: GRR and NRR
preset.subtitle: Statistics · Population statistics

preset.caption: Set the fertility (children per woman), the share of girls among births and the average survival ratio. The dot shows the NRR against the replacement level 1.

Out of 1000 babies born together, lₓ are still alive at age x (yellow). The area under the curve to the right of x is Tₓ, the total years they will still live, so the expectation of life is eₓ = Tₓ/lₓ. Raise the mortality level and watch the curve fall earlier.
preset.title: A life table curve
preset.subtitle: Statistics · Population statistics

preset.caption: Enter one row of a life table: the number alive at x and at x + 1, and Tₓ. The readouts give the other columns.

preset.caption: Price of rice (₹/kg): 30, 32, 35, 38, 40 and p₂₀₂₄. Each bar is p₁/p₀ × 100 on the chosen base year.

Rice ₹30 → p₁ per kg, milk ₹40 → ₹50 per litre, cloth ₹100 → ₹110 per metre.
preset.title: The unit test
preset.subtitle: Statistics · Index numbers

preset.caption: The bars are the price relatives of four items. Change the current price of rice and compare the two unweighted indices.

sliders.name: r
sliders.label: Rise in the price of A

preset.caption: Two goods. Raise the price of A and let families buy less of it (the cut). Laspeyres weights prices by base quantities, so it ignores the cut and tends to overstate the price rise; Paasche uses current quantities and tends to understate it. Fisher’s ideal index lies between them.
preset.title: Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher
preset.subtitle: Statistics · Index numbers

preset.caption: Change this year's quantities of rice and milk. Laspeyres' index uses base quantities and stays fixed; Paasche's and Fisher's move.
Change this year's quantity of rice. Laspeyres' P₀₁ × P₁₀ moves away from 1; Fisher's stays exactly 1 and also passes the factor reversal test.

readouts.label: Wage needed to keep the real wage

preset.caption: Set a worker’s wage in the base year, the consumer price index now, and the money wage now. The real wage is money wage × 100 ÷ CPI: the wage in base-year rupees. The coin shrinks with the purchasing power of the rupee, 100 ÷ CPI.
preset.title: Real wages and the CPI
preset.subtitle: Statistics · Index numbers

preset.caption: The pie shows the budget weights. Change the weight of food (index 180) and the money wage; watch the CPI and the real wage.
Build a time series from its parts. Change the trend slope, the seasonal swing and the cyclical swing (a 4-year cycle).
The trend line passes through the two semi-averages, plotted at the middle years 2 and 5 of a six-year series. Move the averages.
A series with a trend and a cycle of k years. The orange curve is its m-year moving average. When m equals k, the cycle disappears.

readouts.label: Sum of squared errors Σ(y − a − bX)²

preset.caption: Data: 50, 55, 57, 60, 63, 67, 68 for X = −3 … 3. Try your own a and b and watch the sum of squared errors. The least-squares line is a = 60, b = 3.
Data: 10, 13, 15, 23, 30 at X = −2 … 2. Adjust a, b and c to fit the parabola, and watch the error. Then compare with the least-squares values.
The yellow curve is the true (unknown) function. A straight line joins two known points a and b. Where the curve bends, the straight-line estimate is poor.

readouts.label: Simple average of y₁ and y₃

preset.caption: Set the four known values y₀, y₁, y₃, y₄. The middle bar is the estimate of y₂ from Δ⁴y₀ = 0.
The curve is Newton's interpolating polynomial through the four census points. Move the year and read the estimate.

title: Lagrange's curve through any four points

readouts.label: Coefficient sum L₀ + L₁ + L₂ at 30

preset.caption: The curve is the Lagrange polynomial through (20, 230), (25, m) and (35, 345). Change the middle premium m and read the estimate at age 30.

preset.title: Heads in 3 tosses: p.m.f. and F(x)

preset.caption: X = number of heads in two tosses of a coin with P(head) = p. The bars are the probability mass function.

title: Probability is area under the density

preset.title: Probability is area under the density
preset.subtitle: Statistics · Random variables
preset.caption: Choose a density and drag the two handles a and b. P(a < X < b) is the shaded area under f(x); the whole area is 1. Pull the handles together: the area of a single point is 0, so P(X = a) = 0 for a continuous variable.
The density f(x) = 2x/a² on 0 ≤ x ≤ a (zero elsewhere). Change a and the cut-off c, and read the probabilities.

readouts.label: Loss L that makes the game fair

preset.caption: Two fair coins: you win W₂ for two heads and W₁ for one head, and lose L for no head. The bars are gain × probability; the readout is the expected gain.
X takes 0, 1, 2, 3 with probabilities 0.1, 0.3, 0.4, 0.2 (mean 1.7, variance 0.81). Make Y = aX + b and read its mean and spread.
A distribution on 0, 1, 2, 3 with P(X = x) = C(3, x) pˣ(1 − p)³⁻ˣ. Change p and watch the shape measures.
X ~ B(6, p): the number of successes in 6 trials. Move p and watch the shape, mean and variance.

title: Poisson as a limit of the binomial

preset.caption: X ~ Poisson(λ). Slide λ and watch the distribution spread out and become more symmetric.
Geometric distribution: failures before the first success. Slide p.

title: The normal curve and its areas

preset.caption: N(μ, σ²) in yellow against the standard normal N(0, 1) in blue. Slide μ and σ.
Standard normal curve with a movable cut-off. Choose x, μ and σ; the readouts give z and the areas.

title: A Z test, sample after sample

preset.caption: Z test for a mean: set the sample mean, μ₀, σ and n. The red line marks your Z on the standard normal curve.
Paired t-test: set the mean difference, its s.d. and the number of pairs. The red line marks t on the t curve with n − 1 d.f.
Chi-square test for a variance: set n, s² and σ₀². The red line marks χ² = (n − 1)s²/σ₀² on the χ² curve with n − 1 d.f.
